## A standard docs layout

The sidebar now works like the documentation sites readers know.

- **Folders are sections.** Each folder under your pages becomes a sidebar section that folds open; a folder inside a folder becomes a sub-section, as deep as you nest them.
- **The sections holding the current page start open**, the page is highlighted, and a breadcrumb trail above its title links back up. On the home page, the top-level sections are open.
- **Section names and order:** a folder's `index.md` names its section, otherwise the folder name does (`get-started` becomes "Get started"). Sections sort by the lowest `order:` inside them, so numbering pages across the site (1, 2 in Get started; 10, 11 in Guides) orders the sections too.
- **Generated reference pages** join your `reference/` folder, after your own pages there.
- **Previous and next links** follow the sidebar from top to bottom.
- **The agent lays new docs out in sections** (get started, guides, reference, concepts) and shows the folder tree in its outline.

indoc's own docs now use this layout: https://byabasaija.github.io/indoc/

### Upgrading

- **Flat docs keep working** as before, just without sections. To get sections, move pages into folders, then run `indoc bundle`. Until you do, `indoc check` reports the moved pages as removed and new.
- **Ejected sidebar:** if you ran `indoc theme eject sidebar` on 0.6, delete `.indoc/theme/sidebar.html` and eject it again. The sidebar's data changed shape (`.Nav` is now a tree of items with `Children`), so the old copy no longer builds.
